scope: 28 calendar.ts local callables mapped to frozen Temporal steps or prose. Twenty-seven gain comments with one shared sign-check annotation. One existing comment is reconciled. Five structural helpers lack an exact inline step.
source_comparison: Frozen Temporal proposal via checklist rows. ECMA-262 remains requested authority.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.26 step 1.b.
// Reuse the prepared ISO year, month, month code and day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The cache stores only these four ISO fields by epoch day and may seed them from already prepared values. date-core.ts uses them in ISO field getters. Other Calendar Date Record fields are projected separately.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §9.5.4 step 2.
// Compute a nonnegative month residue for ISO year-month balancing.
reviewed_rows.evidence: addYearMonth uses this private modulo expression for fixed-month calendars; in ISO the divisor is exactly twelve. This arrow does not compute the year carry.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.5.12 steps 1, 2, §5.5.4 steps 3, 4.
// Check the inclusive epoch-day interval for a date at noon.
reviewed_rows.evidence: An integral day at noon lies strictly inside the frozen local date-time bounds exactly for days −100000001 through 100000000. The separate safe-integer check is a provider input guard.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.5.7 steps 1.a, 1.c, 2.b.
// Clamp or reject a prepared month or day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rejects noninteger inputs as an adapter guard. For caller-supplied day or month limits, reject fails outside the interval and constrain clamps. Calendar selection and the complete date record stay outside.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.3.11 step 3, §3.3.16 step 3.
// Look up the first epoch day of the calendar year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns the Chinese/Dangi table start, an in-range Umm al-Qura start or Islamic civil fallback, or an arithmetic start. calendarStartOfYear feeds dateProperty's non-ISO ordinal and length calculations. No public getter action.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.3.11 step 3, §3.3.16 step 3.
// Select the provider for the calendar year start.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks prepared calendar and year, then uses native or fallback year starts. date-core.ts subtracts the result to derive dayOfYear or daysInYear on its compositional path. Provider availability stays profile-specific.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.3.17 step 3.
// Read the selected calendar's month count for a year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns native month count or arithmetic/table count, including possible lunisolar intercalation. The same value supplies private validation and dateProperty's monthsInYear projection.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.3.15 step 3, §3.5.7 step 1.b.
// Read the prepared calendar month length.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches native or validates the local month index and selects table/arithmetic length. date-core.ts projects it and conversion uses it for day limits. Extended chronology/fallback premise remains profile-specific.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.2.2 steps 2, 3.a, 4, §12.3.26 step 2.
// Encode the month code after projecting its calendar index.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Lunisolar path subtracts the inserted leap slot from subsequent ordinals and emits the leap suffix on that month. Other calendars delegate to ArithmeticCalendarMonthCode. ISO and non-ISO complete date records remain composed elsewhere.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.22 step 2, §12.3.21 prose.
// Resolve a prepared non-ISO month code for the selected year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Handles inserted Chinese/Dangi or Hebrew leap months and the M13 arithmetic calendar forms. Reject mode can fail when the leap code is absent. The complete overflow policy and calendar conversion remain in callers.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.31 steps 1.h.i, 1.h.ii, 1.h.iii, 1.h.iv.
// Read a prepared ISO month code and reject out-of-range forms.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Recognizes three ASCII units M01–M12 and returns the month. Rejects leap and unsupported numeric forms. Matching to an independently supplied numeric month happens in the caller.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.12 steps 2, 3, §12.3.31 steps 1.g, 1.h.v.
// Convert prepared ISO fields and check the resulting day bounds.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Checks missing month representations, code/number agreement and selected overflow before arithmetic, or delegates to native ISO conversion. Both paths apply dayCheck. Public reads and required year/day checks are upstream.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.22 steps 1.b, 2.
// Convert prepared calendar fields to an epoch day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches native or resolves bounded month/day and converts through arithmetic or table chronology. Deliberate raw range permits internal/reference-date paths. Calendar fields prep and standard date result bounds stay with callers.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.12 steps 2, 3.
// Apply the normal date bounds after calendar conversion.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Composes raw prepared date conversion with exact dayCheck. Callers own CalendarResolveFields and public access ordering.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.26 steps 1.b, 2.
// Project a bounded epoch day into calendar date fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Applies ordinary day bound before delegating the raw year/month/month code/day projection. This is not the complete Calendar Date Record.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.26 steps 1.b, 2, §12.3.25 prose.
// Project an epoch day using native, arithmetic or table chronology.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Selects native or calendar-specific projection and returns year, month, code and day. The ±110000000 input limit is a private guard for projections, not the normative PlainDate bound.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §9.5.4 steps 1, 2, §12.3.7 step 2.a.
// Balance the prepared ISO or non-ISO year and month.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Fixed-month path adds a serialized month offset then decomposes it; ISO uses twelve. Lunisolar and Hebrew preserve calendar month identity across variable-year length. No day regulation here.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.7 steps 1.a, 1.b, 1.d, 2.a.
// Add a date duration through native or fallback chronology.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Resolves the starting fields then delegates native or raw calendar arithmetic and reprojects fields. The raw helper does not impose the full public date-range check.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.7 steps 1.a, 1.b, 1.c, 1.d, 2.a.
// Balance year and month, regulate the day and add weeks and days.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Normalizes the four prepared duration fields, rejects mixed signs, balances year/month, re-regulates original day and adds seven times weeks plus days. Normal calendar limits and public duration conversion are separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §7.5.9 step 1, §7.5.16 steps 2.b and 2.c.
// Check both signs in the prepared date-duration fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Left predicate identifies a negative field. Joint use with the matching positive predicate rejects mixed signs for four prepared date fields, not the whole IsValidDuration algorithm.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §7.5.9 step 1, §7.5.16 steps 2.b and 2.c.
// Check both signs in the prepared date-duration fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Right predicate identifies a positive field. Both occurrences share a line but have independent AST columns. Remaining duration invariants stay upstream.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.7 steps 1.a, 1.b, 1.d, 2.a.
// Carry normalized calendar arithmetic back as an epoch day and fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Starts from already projected normalized fields, forwards through native or fallback arithmetic, and returns paired epoch and projected date. date-core and PlainYearMonth callers retain final limits.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.7 steps 3, 4.
// Bound the calendar addition result before returning its fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: No production caller found outside this helper's declaration. Calendar tests and arithmetic oracle exercise the exact dayCheck guard and return. This annotation describes only that invariant.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.9 steps 3.e.ii, 4, §12.3.8 prose.
// Provide serial month indices for calendar difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Physical month numbering supports private month difference between the selected base and end. The ISO and non-ISO branches in calendarDateUntilRaw handle prefix selection/comparison separately.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §12.3.9 steps 2, 3.k, 4.
// Compute the date duration for the prepared endpoints and largest unit.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Selects native or fallback chronology strategy. Fallback zeroes equal endpoints, adjusts year/month prefix against unregulated components and distributes remainder. Match is caller and algorithm dependency, without full step equivalence.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.5.6 steps 4, 7, 8, §12.3.9 steps 3.c.ii, 3.e.ii.
// Compare the candidate prefix with the endpoint before day clamping.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Compares proposed year/month code and original day, then balanced year/month plus original day. Used by both year and month prefix checks. Other ISODateSurpasses branches and non-ISO chronology remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation:
// Temporal comparison §3.3.4 step 3, §3.3.5 step 3.
// Project era and era year from the private calendar date.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches native or arithmetic/table projection over prepared epoch and calendar. Nonextended native path checks day bounds. Public branding and complete CalendarISOToDate projection stay outside.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Temporal comparison §12.3.31 step2.a / §12.3.30: normalize private era data.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Existing inline comment covers private non-ISO era normalization. Fallback handles Japanese era offsets, Ethiopic alias and civil era polarity. Typed native provider may own this conversion. Public field resolution and consistency checks belong elsewhere.

no_exact_step_rows.evidence: Checks Number.isSafeInteger for prepared private adapter values. Used for dates, counters and duration components. Neither public ToInteger nor IsValidDuration imposes this shared safe-integer check at one exact step.

Checks finite safe integer and private ±400000 year window. The exact ISODateWithinLimits/ISOYearMonthWithinLimits rules use separate represented dates and months. This guard prevents arithmetic outside the local provider domain and cannot stand in for either normative bound.

Checks exact lowercase internal CalendarId membership. Public calendar identifier parser, alias normalization and canonicalization run upstream. No frozen algorithm step calls for a second generic whitelist check at these private provider entry points.
Checks the already prepared Overflow union and throws RangeError for an invalid internal token. Public option getters and RegulateISODate/CalendarDateToISO own different operations.

Only calendar.test.ts consumes it. It returns subtraction of two prepared bounded epoch days, with no largestUnit, year or month prefix handling or public difference path. Evidence supports a test assertion helper, not an exact production caller step.

validation.result: 5 Bazel targets passed in the same validation batch.
